findings.evidence: The PR itself works around the mismatch at every existing call site: Basic.lean:107-112 and 195 and 212 use `simpa using (... hb 0 lambda hlam x)`, Basic.lean:131 needs `convert S.norm_pow_mul_resolvent_integrand_le hb 0 lambda x ht using 1 <;> ring_nf`, and Identity.lean:113-118 had to add `pow_zero, one_mul` to its `simp only` set.
findings.fix: Add public `n = 0` corollaries in the shape of `resolvent_apply` — e.g. `StronglyContinuousSemigroup.integrableOn_resolvent_integrand (hb) (lambda) (hlam) (x) : IntegrableOn (fun t => Real.exp (-(lambda * t)) • S.realOperator t x) (Set.Ioi 0)` and `norm_resolvent_integrand_le` — proved by `simpa using ... 0 ...`, and use them at the five in-repo sites. These are not compatibility aliases for the deleted `integrable_resolvent_integrand`: they are distinct, simp-normal statements about the post-PR definition of `resolvent`.
findings.issue: `integrableOn_pow_mul_resolvent_integrand` (line 78) and `norm_pow_mul_resolvent_integrand_le` (line 56) state the integrand as `(t ^ n * Real.exp (-(lambda * t))) • S.realOperator t x`, but `resolvent` (line 103) and `resolvent_apply`/`resolventFun_apply` (lines 147, 344) present it as `Real.exp (-(lambda * t)) • S.realOperator t x`. The `n = 0` instance no longer matches syntactically, so the characteristic integrability/bound facts for the resolvent's own defining integral are unavailable to `exact`/`rw`; every consumer must rediscover the `n`-form and normalize by hand.

summary: Prior findings are fixed: the exponent is now simp-normal `-(lambda * t)` and the contraction/general resolvent bridge is public. Remaining: generalizing the integrand lemmas over `n` left no lemma stated in the shape of `resolvent_apply`, so the defining integral's integrability and norm bound are no longer directly usable.
